findings.title: Shared mutable default timestamp
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` shares the same timestamp. The fix is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence is stale/incorrect `queued` values for all sources and broken ordering/expiry logic if ever used.

findings.title: to_dict returns non-JSON-serializable datetime for Celery
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py, `to_dict()` uses `asdict()` which returns the raw `datetime` object for `queued`. Callers in src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py pass this dict as `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`, which must be JSON-serializable for Celery. This will raise a serialization error and break outbound assignee sync entirely when a source is present. Serialize to ISO string instead.

findings.title: from_dict does not parse serialized datetime
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py, `from_dict()` does `cls(**input_dict)` directly. After a JSON round-trip `queued` will be a string, not a `datetime`, so the resulting object violates its type and `to_dict`/`from_dict` are not symmetric. It also silently accepts extra/missing keys via TypeError handling. Consequence is type confusion, potential crashes in code expecting datetime, and inability to reliably rehydrate the Celery payload.

findings.title: should_sync signature change breaks existing overrides
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py, `should_sync(self, attribute, sync_source=None)` adds a required positional path that callers like `sync_assignee_outbound` now use with two arguments. Any existing IssueBasicIntegration/IssueSyncIntegration subclass overriding `should_sync(self, attribute)` with the old single-arg signature will raise TypeError when called. Consequence is runtime crashes for third-party or un-updated integrations. Keep backward compatibility with *args/**kwargs or defensive calling.

findings.title: Inconsistent outbound signatures for assignment_source
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py, `sync_status_outbound` was given an explicit `assignment_source` parameter but `sync_assignee_outbound` was left as `**kwargs` only, while src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. Implementations that define strict signatures without **kwargs will fail, and static typing/lint cannot catch the assignee case. Consequence is potential TypeError and confusing asymmetry between status and assignee sync paths. Add the explicit parameter to both abstract methods.
